issues.legal_issue: An interim application connected with arbitration is a suit for land for territorial-jurisdiction purposes when its substance requires determination of competing claims to possession of land and the requested relief would affect land outside the court’s territorial limits.
material_facts: The parties’ agreements concerned development of land and gave the developer interests in the project and possession of the site.
After termination of the agreements, each party asserted that it possessed the land; the developer also claimed that buildings and construction work had been completed or commenced there.

The developer’s interim application sought to prevent the landowner from entering or dealing with the property and from interfering with the developer’s asserted possession and construction machinery.
The land was outside the territorial limits of the court where the interim application was filed.
issues.conclusion: The application was, in substance, a suit for land because determining the requested relief required determining possession and would affect the land. The court where the application was filed therefore lacked territorial jurisdiction, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent, a suit for land may be received and tried only if the land is within the court’s local limits. Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 permits applications for interim measures, including injunctions, but does not displace that territorial limitation. Section 120 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 makes Sections 16, 17 and 20 inapplicable to the High Court’s original civil jurisdiction. Whether a matter is a suit for land is determined from the substance of the claim and the relief sought: it is one where relief relates to title to or delivery of possession of land, or where the court must decide conflicting claims to the land and its order would affect it. The Court relied on Moolji Jaitha & Co. v. Khandesh Spinning & Weaving Mills Co. Ltd., Adcon Electronics Pvt. Ltd. v. Daulat and Excel Dealcomm Pvt. Ltd. v. Asset Reconstruction Co. (India) Ltd.

rule.if: arbitration_interim_proceeding and possession_is_disputed and claim_requires_possession_determination and requested_relief_affects_land and land_outside_court_territory

predicates.arbitration_interim_proceeding: A party sought interim relief from a court in connection with an arbitration.
predicates.possession_is_disputed: The parties made conflicting assertions about who possessed the land.
predicates.claim_requires_possession_determination: Resolving the requested relief required the court to determine which party was entitled to possession of the land.
predicates.requested_relief_affects_land: The applicant sought relief that would protect or restrict entry upon, possession of, or dealings with the land.
predicates.land_outside_court_territory: The land affected by the requested relief was outside the territorial limits of the court.

issues.definition: When an arbitration-related interim application requires determination of disputed possession, seeks relief affecting the land, and concerns land outside the court’s territorial limits, the court lacks territorial jurisdiction.
